title: refactor(app-shell): split StudioDesignSurface.tsx by responsibility
body:
repo:objectstack#5 · os-bill · session_01Utp6CbL6Nn3scsU8yvLyU4
Fixes #37553
Clause-②: no
Metadata-protocol: none

## 维护者速读

- 用户能看到什么变化：没有变化，Studio 的每个页面、按钮、文案和地址都和合并前一样；这是工程内部的拆文件，用户无感。
- 为什么做：属于 App Studio 改版第一阶段的收尾，Studio 主框架这个一千五百多行的大文件被拆成八个按职责划分的小文件，第二阶段改界面时几张卡不必再排队改同一个文件。
- 出错会怎样：如果拆的时候漏接了某条线，Studio 的发布、保存、右侧栏或页面切换会出问题；整个改动只是搬代码，可以直接撤回。
- 要你做什么：本次改动超过三千行（搬移的代码两头都算），按规则合并前需要你批准一次。

## What changes

`ui/packages/app-shell/src/views/studio-design/StudioDesignSurface.tsx` goes from **1,550** lines (at `e491fce2c7`) to **383**. It keeps its exports, its props and its default export, and now only composes: it calls the hooks below in the order their lines stood, then draws the frame with the page inside it.

| Module | Lines | Owns |
|---|---:|---|
| `studioSurfaceScope.ts` | 338 | The scope: the route segment read as a package, `~org` or `~all`; the package-list facts (writable, name, missing, a read-only base's facts and its `.custom` pair); the base's customization; the package's apps |
| `studioSurfaceSave.ts` | 75 | The save-entry plumbing: the dirty-pillar, held-edit and Save-bar bits, the one departure question, the tab-close prompt, the unsaved-edits registration |
| `studioSurfaceDrafts.tsx` | 203 | The drafts state: the Pending changes sheet and its `?changes=review` door, the publish and draft-save nonces, the pending ledger behind the badges and the Pending tab, the refusals a publish keeps on its entries |
| `studioSurfacePublish.ts` | 338 | The publish every door runs (batch door, or flow by flow in `~org`), its toasts and the backfill receipt |
| `studioSurfaceRightSlot.tsx` | 225 | The right slot and the assistant: the host gate, open and mode state, the shortcut, the title row's assistant control, the slot element with the copilot |
| `studioSurfaceNavigation.tsx` | 164 | The retired-Interfaces landing latch, the host side of `?surface=`, the menu re-entry, the command palette's Studio scope |
| `StudioSurfaceFrame.tsx` | 270 | The frame: the providers, the two columns (the menu mount with its top rows, the pillars host), the strips, the slot mount, the review sheet, the palette. Stateless; the page is `children` |
| `StudioSurfacePage.tsx` | 215 | The page beside the menu: the All metadata area, 概览 Overview with its Pending tab, the sharing overview, the not-found states. Stateless |

Every module is under 400 lines.

**How it was cut.** Eight move commits, one per module, each a verbatim move of a contiguous block into a hook or a component with the body calling it where the block stood. No rename. Two follow-up commits, kept apart from the moves: one lists five `useState` setters in the dependency arrays of the moved callbacks that now receive them across a module boundary (`onPackageChanged`, `onPackageRenamed`, `onDraftSaved`, `requestSurface`, `doPublish`), and one adds a map of the split to the surface's header comment.

**What stays the same, and why it holds.**

- **Hook and effect order.** The hooks are called in the order their lines stood, so every effect, subscription and fetch starts in the same order as before. The one reordering is among a `useRef` and five `useCallback` / `useMemo` calls (the publish now follows the ledger's callbacks), which run no effect.
- **The rendered tree.** `StudioSurfaceFrame` and `StudioSurfacePage` hold no hooks and no state. They add two component layers with constant types, so nothing remounts, and every keyed element (`key={packageId}`, `key={scopeSegment}`) keeps its key under the same parent. The DOM is the same.
- **The dependency-array commit.** A `useState` setter's identity never changes, so adding one to a dependency list re-creates no callback. Without it, `react-hooks/exhaustive-deps` adds five new warnings, because it cannot see that a setter passed from another module is stable. With it, the files carry the warnings the original carried.

**Tests.** ~~No test file is edited, added or deleted.~~ No test is added or deleted. Two source-reading tests gain list entries only (patch round, below); no assertion changes. No `vi.mock` needed re-pointing: the new modules import the same module paths the surface imported, so every path mock still applies, and nothing mocked the surface itself.

## Read first (riskiest first)

1. `studioSurfacePublish.ts`, `useStudioPublishAction`: the 220-line publish moved whole. The risk is the parameter list, since every state setter and value it closed over is now passed in.
2. `StudioDesignSurface.tsx`, the body of `StudioDesignSurfaceBody`: the hook call order is what keeps the effect order. Compare it with the order of the blocks in the base file.
3. `StudioSurfaceFrame.tsx`: the JSX is verbatim. The page went to `{children}`, the right slot to `{rightSlot}`.

## Tests

All of these ran at head `6a7446c9a4`, the final commit, through the shared verification lock.

- **The full app-shell suite, green.** `pnpm --filter @object-ui/app-shell test --maxWorkers=2` ran **2,456 files passed, 1 skipped (2,457)** and **23,816 tests passed, 9 skipped**. The skips were already there: ~~no test file is touched~~ this run, at `6a7446c9a4`, was before the patch round, and no test file had been touched yet.
- **The type-check, green.** `pnpm --filter @object-ui/app-shell type-check` is both programs, `tsc --noEmit` and `tsc -p tsconfig.test.json`. I also checked that the program sees the new modules: a stray prop added to `StudioSurfaceFrame.tsx` was reported as TS2339, and the file was then restored from HEAD.
- **Lint.** eslint on the nine files gives 0 errors and 8 warnings with `--no-inline-config`: 2 `exhaustive-deps`, 1 `only-export-components` and 5 `set-state-in-effect`. Those are the same kinds and counts the base file gives over the same code. With inline config on, 0 errors: no `eslint-disable` went stale.

**Console E2E: not run locally.** It needs a built Console, and the live specs also need a running backend, which is more than this shared container carries next to the suite. CI's `Build & E2E UI` and `Live E2E UI` jobs give the verdict. The specs that drive this surface are `ui/e2e/live/studio-editor.spec.ts`, `studio-object-designer.spec.ts`, `studio-customize-journey.spec.ts` and `studio-detail-save-at-once.spec.ts`. The three `ui/e2e/studio-*.spec.ts` specs read other files (`StudioItemHeader.tsx`, `StudioMenu.tsx`, `StudioDetailHeader.tsx`), and this change does not touch them.

## Acceptance notes

- **The change is over the 3,000-line mark** (+2,028 / −1,367 = 3,395, the move counted on both sides). AGENTS.md multi-agent discipline §7 (c) applies: it lands on an authorized approval or by the maintainer's merge.
- **Two source-reading tests have file lists that the moved bodies are not on.** I left both alone because they are outside this card's file fence. `homeRecoveryRedirectsFollowDeclaration-7373.test.ts` (`alsoReads` for the Studio site) and `ui/scripts/__tests__/spec-symbol-ledger-app-shell-7265.test.ts` (`SITES`) each read `StudioDesignSurface.tsx` plus the modules earlier move-only splits cut out of it. The second file's header records the ruling that "a moved body stays in the reading list". Both stay green, because the moved code holds no launcher literal and no spec-named declaration. But until the eight new paths are added, neither test reads the moved code. That is two list additions with no change to any assertion, for whoever owns those files.
- The base file had a stale comment on its imports (`objectui#11773`, `objectstack#26858`) above an import that no longer matched it. It stays where it was.
- A comment block on the import of the draft-envelope reader moved with that import into `studioSurfacePublish.ts`.

- **Patch round** (claim amendment 7205603061, which widened the fence to two source-reading tests for list additions only). Commit `9828b29963` adds the eight new `studio-design/` module paths to `alsoReads` for the Studio site in `homeRecoveryRedirectsFollowDeclaration-7373.test.ts`, and to `SITES` in `ui/scripts/__tests__/spec-symbol-ledger-app-shell-7265.test.ts`. That is +16 / −0, and no assertion changed. Both tests pass (2 files, 49 tests).
  - Ablation via `scripts/ablation-replace.mjs`, with each restore checked against HEAD. A launcher literal injected into `studioSurfaceNavigation.tsx` turns the Studio site's "does not hard-code the launcher path" case red; with that path also dropped from `alsoReads`, the file is green (15/15). A local `type AppLike` injected into `studioSurfacePublish.ts` turns its rule-1 case red; with that path dropped from `SITES`, the file is green (33/33). Each list entry is what brings the moved code under the scan.
  - `origin/main` was merged once (`fd1a2e0900`). There was no conflict and nothing under `studio-design/` changed.

## Verification

Two-minute check: `git diff e491fce2c7 HEAD --color-moved=zebra -- ui/packages/app-shell/src/views/studio-design/` shows almost every removed line coming back as a moved line. The lines that do not are imports, the `export` keyword on two helpers, the five dependency arrays, and the four wrapper lines where a JSX expression became a `return` or a `const`.

<details><summary>How much of the split is a verbatim move</summary>

A script compared every line of the base file (trimmed) with the nine files after the split. Every original line outside the import blocks reappears verbatim, with seven exceptions, each on purpose:

- `publishRefusalKey` and `NO_PUBLISH_REFUSALS` gain `export`.
- Three dependency arrays gain a setter (the commit kept apart from the moves). Two more did too, but their old spelling, `}, []);`, occurs elsewhere in the file, so the script cannot flag it.
- The keyed-pillars JSX comment lost its braces when it became a block comment above `return`.
- `{allScope ? (` became `return allScope ? (`.
- `{slotHost && (` became `const rightSlot = slotHost && (`.

Of the 2,211 lines after the split, 1,612 match an original line. The rest are imports, module headers, hook signatures, return objects, and the props the frame and the page receive.

</details>
